readme:
# Ballerina Workflow Library

The `ballerina/workflow` library provides durable, fault-tolerant workflow orchestration for Ballerina applications. It lets you define long-running business processes — spanning minutes, hours, or days — that automatically recover from crashes and process restarts without losing progress.

## Overview

Workflows and activities are ordinary Ballerina functions:

- **`@workflow:Workflow`** — A durable function that orchestrates a business process. The runtime checkpoints every step and replays recorded history to recover from failures.
- **`@workflow:Activity`** — A function that performs a single non-deterministic operation (API call, database query, email send). Once an activity completes, its result is recorded and never re-executed during replay.

```ballerina
import ballerina/workflow;

@workflow:Activity
function checkInventory(string item) returns boolean|error {
    // Call external inventory API
    return true;
}

@workflow:Workflow
function processOrder(workflow:Context ctx, OrderRequest request) returns OrderResult|error {
    boolean inStock = check ctx->callActivity(checkInventory, {"item": request.item});
    if !inStock {
        return {orderId: request.orderId, status: "OUT_OF_STOCK"};
    }
    return {orderId: request.orderId, status: "COMPLETED"};
}
```

## Authoring guidelines

- Workflow functions must contain only orchestration logic (control flow and waiting for data). All business logic and non-deterministic operations - database calls, external API calls, I/O - belong in activity functions.
- Activities must be invoked through `ctx->callActivity(...)` from within a workflow function. Calling an activity function directly is a compile-time error.
- When calling an activity, pass its arguments as a record whose keys exactly match the activity function's parameter names - for example, `ctx->callActivity(checkInventory, {"item": request.item})` for `function checkInventory(string item)`.
- When using the Ballerina Integrator tooling, place all `@workflow:Workflow` and `@workflow:Activity` functions in the project's `functions.bal` file.
- Store the workflow ID returned by `workflow:run()` so that later `workflow:sendData()` calls can be routed to the correct running instance.

## Starting a Workflow

Use `workflow:run()` to start a workflow instance from any entry point — HTTP service, scheduled job, message consumer, or `main`:

```ballerina
string workflowId = check workflow:run(processOrder, {orderId: "ORD-001", item: "laptop"});
```

## Receiving External Data

A workflow can pause and wait for external input — approvals, payment confirmations, user decisions — using future-based event records. Send data to a running workflow with `workflow:sendData()`:

```ballerina
// In the workflow — wait for a human decision
ApprovalDecision decision = check wait events.approval;

// From outside — deliver the decision
check workflow:sendData(processOrder, workflowId, "approval", {approverId: "mgr-1", approved: true});
```

### Multi-Future Waits with `ctx->await`

Use `ctx->await` to wait for multiple futures at once, with optional quorum and timeout:

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Wait for all | `ctx->await([f1, f2])` |
| Wait for any (first wins) | `ctx->await([f1, f2], 1)` |
| Quorum (N of M) | `ctx->await([f1, f2, f3], 2)` |
| With deadline | `ctx->await([f1, f2], timeout = {hours: 48})` |

## Error Handling

Activity errors are returned as plain Ballerina values. The workflow decides what happens next:

```ballerina
string|error result = ctx->callActivity(chargeCard, {"amount": input.amount});
if result is error {
    // retry with a different card, fall back, or compensate
}
```

Enable automatic retries for transient failures:

```ballerina
string result = check ctx->callActivity(chargeCard, {"amount": input.amount},
    retryOnError = true, maxRetries = 3);
```

## Configuration

Add a `Config.toml` to your project. For local development with no server:

```toml
[ballerina.workflow]
mode = "IN_MEMORY"
```

For production, connect to a Temporal server:

```toml
[ballerina.workflow]
mode = "TEMPORAL"
temporalHost = "localhost"
temporalPort = 7233
namespace = "default"
taskQueue = "my-task-queue"
```

typeDefs.name: SINGLE_EVENT
typeDefs.description:
The channel is consumed exactly once per run. Declare this only when the
channel receives a single event per agent instance — a later event on the
channel is never consumed

typeDefs.name: MULTI_EVENT
NoAutomaticRetry
typeDefs.description:
No automatic retry by the engine. Errors from the activity are returned
directly to the caller. This is the default behaviour when no `retryPolicy`
is specified. Note that an AI agent may still decide to call the activity
again from its own reasoning — this policy only disables engine-driven
retries.

typeDefs.description: Deprecated alias of `NoAutomaticRetry`.

typeDefs.name: EventDecl
typeDefs.description:
A named event channel of a durable agent. `request`/`response` capture both
sides' types and the channel's duplexity: a `response` type declares a duplex
(request-response) channel whose turn answers are read with
`getDataResult`/`waitForDataResult`; a nil `response` declares a one-way
channel — data flows in, no result is read back.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The channel name (unique across all of the agent's capabilities)

fields.name: request
fields.description: Type of the payload sent to the agent on this channel

fields.name: response
fields.description: Type of the agent's reply for this channel; `()` for one-way channels

fields.name: cardinality
fields.description:
Business cardinality of the channel: re-armed per turn
(`MULTI_EVENT`, the default) or consumed once (`SINGLE_EVENT`)

typeDefs.name: ActivityDecl
typeDefs.description:
An activity capability of a durable agent, with optional gating and retry config.
For the no-config case pass the bare `@workflow:Activity` function instead.

fields.name: activity
fields.description: The `@workflow:Activity` function

fields.name: name
fields.description: Tool name advertised to the model; defaults to the function name

fields.name: description
fields.description:
Tool description advertised to the model; defaults to the
function's doc comment

fields.name: bindings
fields.description:
Fixed arguments partially applied to the activity (e.g. a
`connection`), hidden from the model: only the remaining data
parameters appear in the tool's schema. Client objects are bound
by referencing their module-level `final` variable

fields.name: requiresApproval
fields.description: When `true`, a `PRE_RUN` review activity gates every call

fields.name: userRoles
fields.description: Role(s) permitted to decide reviews of this activity

fields.name: retryPolicy
fields.description: Retry behaviour on failure, as for `ctx->callActivity`

typeDefs.name: AutoRetry
typeDefs.description:
Automatic retry configuration. When the activity fails, it is automatically
retried according to the configured backoff policy.

fields.name: maxRetries
fields.description: Maximum retry attempts (default: 3)

fields.name: retryDelay
fields.description: Initial delay in seconds before the first retry (default: 1.0)

fields.name: retryBackoff
fields.description: Multiplier applied to delay after each retry (default: 2.0)

fields.name: maxRetryDelay
fields.description: Cap on the delay between retries, in seconds

typeDefs.name: HumanReview
typeDefs.description:
Human-review retry policy: the role(s) permitted to decide the retry review.
Passing a role name (or list of role names) as the `retryPolicy` creates a
review task on activity failure so a matching human can decide to retry,
retry with different input, or permanently fail. The task name is derived
automatically from the activity being called.

An AI tool capability of a durable agent, with optional gating config. For the
no-config case pass the `ai:ToolConfig`/`ai:BaseToolKit`/`@ai:AgentTool` function
directly.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: The tool: an `@ai:AgentTool` function, an `ai:ToolConfig`, or a toolkit

fields.name: requiresApproval
fields.description: When `true`, a `PRE_RUN` review activity gates every call

fields.name: userRoles
fields.description: Role(s) permitted to decide reviews of this tool

fields.name: name
fields.description: The task name (unique across all of the agent's capabilities)

fields.name: roles

A peer durable agent advertised to this agent's model as a delegable tool.
The framework runs the peer as a Temporal child workflow.

fields.name: agent

fields.name: description
fields.description: What the peer does, for the model

fields.name: 'wait

typeDefs.name: DurableAgent
typeDefs.description:
Declares the agent. Capabilities are fixed here and registered with the
workflow runtime at module init by the compiler plugin.

functions.name: init
functions.description:
Declares the agent. Capabilities are fixed here and registered with the
workflow runtime at module init by the compiler plugin.

parameters.name: systemPrompt
parameters.description:
The agent's identity: role + instructions (the per-run query
is appended as the user turn by `run`)

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model provider used for the agent's LLM calls

parameters.name: inputType
parameters.description:
The agent's workflow input type, used by `run` and the management
API start. `string` (the default) means the query text itself is
the input; a data type declares a structured `run` input payload
validated against it; `()` declares a no-input agent (started
empty, typically driven by its event channels)

parameters.name: resultType
parameters.description:
When declared, the agent produces a typed final result: as the
reasoning loop concludes, one more durable model call converts the
conversation outcome into this type, and `waitForResult`/`getResult`
return it. `()` keeps the final text response

parameters.name: activities
parameters.description:
`@workflow:Activity` functions, bare or as `ActivityDecl` when
gating/roles/bindings are needed

parameters.name: tools
parameters.description:
AI tools: `@ai:AgentTool` functions, `ai:ToolConfig`s, toolkits, or
`ToolDecl` when gating is needed

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Named event channels with request/response types and cardinality

parameters.name: humanTasks
parameters.description:
Human task capabilities. Capability names share one namespace
across activities, tools, events, human tasks, and peers: a name
claimed twice is rejected when the agent registers, so the
program fails at startup

parameters.name: peers
parameters.description: Peer durable agents advertised as delegable tools

parameters.name: maxIter
parameters.description: Hard cap on reasoning iterations per turn

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The agent's complete configuration

return.description: An error when the configuration is invalid

functions.name: bindAgentName
functions.description:
Binds the agent's stable identity — its module-level variable name — to this
object. Called by the compiler-plugin-generated module-init code; not part of
the public API surface. The first binding wins; later calls are ignored.

parameters.name: agentName
parameters.description: The agent's module-level variable name

functions.name: run
functions.description:
Starts the agent durably and returns the new instance ID — always the ID,
never the result (a durable agent may suspend for days on a human task, so
no caller thread is blocked). Outside a workflow this is a top-level start;
inside a `@workflow:Workflow` the agent runs as a Temporal child workflow.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user turn appended to the agent's system prompt

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Optional structured input for the run

return.description: The new agent instance ID, or an error

functions.name: sendData
functions.description:
Sends an event to a running instance on a declared channel and returns a
correlation token for reading that turn's response.

parameters.name: instanceId
parameters.description: The agent instance ID returned by `run`

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: A channel declared in the agent's `events`

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The payload; must match the channel's declared `request` type

return.description:
A correlation token for `getDataResult`/`waitForDataResult`,
or an error

functions.name: getResult
functions.description:
Returns the final result of an instance if it has finished, without waiting.
While the instance is still working (e.g. suspended on a human task) a
`workflow:AgentBusyError` is returned — check back later, or use `waitForResult`.

parameters.name: instanceId
parameters.description: The agent instance ID returned by `run`

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected result type (inferred from context)

return.description:
The result as `T`, a `workflow:AgentBusyError` while in progress,
or an error

functions.name: getDataResult
functions.description:
Returns the response for a specific `sendData` turn if it is ready, without
waiting. While the turn is unanswered a `workflow:AgentBusyError` is returned.

parameters.name: instanceId
parameters.description: The agent instance ID returned by `run`

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The correlation token returned by `sendData`

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected response type (inferred from context)

return.description:
The turn's response as `T`, a `workflow:AgentBusyError` while
unanswered, or an error

functions.name: waitForResult
functions.description:
Waits until the instance finishes and returns its result. Inside a workflow
this durably suspends the caller (no thread held); from a service it blocks
but is resumable — if the caller crashes, calling again after restart resumes
the wait, because the result lives in history.

parameters.name: instanceId
parameters.description: The agent instance ID returned by `run`

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected result type (inferred from context)

return.description: The result as `T`, or an error

functions.name: waitForDataResult
functions.description:
Waits for a specific `sendData` turn's response (same durability guarantees
as `waitForResult`).

parameters.name: instanceId
parameters.description: The agent instance ID returned by `run`

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The correlation token returned by `sendData`

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected response type (inferred from context)

return.description: The turn's response as `T`, or an error

typeDefs.name: AgentBusyError
typeDefs.description:
Returned by the non-blocking `getResult`/`getDataResult` reads when the agent
instance (or the specific turn) is still in progress — e.g. suspended on a human
task. Check back later, or use the blocking `waitForResult`/`waitForDataResult`
forms, which durably wait and are resumable across crashes.

fields.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at which the timeout was recorded

typeDefs.name: HumanTaskTimeoutError
typeDefs.description:
Returned by `awaitHumanTask` when no human acts within the configured deadline.
Catch with `on fail workflow:HumanTaskTimeoutError e` to run compensation logic.

typeDefs.name: PendingAgentEvent
typeDefs.description:
A data-event turn a durable agent has accepted but not yet answered. Returned
by `getPendingAgentEvents` so callers can rediscover in-flight event turns
after a crash and fetch their answers via `DurableAgent.getDataResult` /
`waitForDataResult`.

fields.name: token
fields.description: The turn's correlation token (as returned by `DurableAgent.sendData`)

fields.name: eventName
fields.description: The event channel the turn was sent on

typeDefs.name: WorkflowBusyError
typeDefs.description:
Returned by the non-blocking `ctx->getChildWorkflowResult` read when the child
workflow is still running (e.g. suspended on a human task). Check back later, or
use the blocking `ctx->waitForChildWorkflow` form, which durably suspends until
the child completes.

clients.name: Context
clients.description:
Workflow execution context providing activity execution, durable sleep,
deterministic time, and multi-future await APIs.

functions.name: init
functions.description:
Creates a workflow execution context wrapping the native context handle.
This constructor is called by the workflow runtime; do not instantiate `Context` directly.

parameters.name: nativeContext
parameters.description: Native context handle from the workflow engine

functions.name: callActivity
functions.description:
Executes an activity function. A completed activity is never re-executed on
workflow replay — its recorded result is reused, even across process crashes
and restarts. A *failed* attempt may run again, however: `AutoRetry` re-executes
the activity automatically and `HumanReview` lets a human rerun it, so make the
activity's side effects idempotent (or deduplicate them) when retries are enabled.

```ballerina
PaymentResult result = check ctx->callActivity(processPayment, args = {"orderId": orderId});
```

parameters.name: activityFunction
parameters.description: The activity function (must have `@Activity`)

parameters.name: args
parameters.description:
Arguments to pass to the activity. Values are normally `anydata`.
Module-level `final` `client object` variables may also be passed for
activity parameters whose declared type is a client object; the
compiler plugin validates the call site and substitutes a
`"connection:<name>"` marker for transport across the workflow
execution boundary.

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected return type (inferred from context)

parameters.name: retryPolicy
parameters.description:
Retry behaviour on failure:
- `()` / `NoAutomaticRetry` (default) — error is returned as-is, no retry.
- `AutoRetry` — automatic backoff retry with configurable attempts and delays.
- `HumanReview` — on failure a review task is created for a human to decide
whether to retry (optionally with new input) or permanently fail the activity.

return.description: The activity result as `T`, or an error

functions.name: sleep
functions.description:
Durable sleep that survives process crashes and restarts. Do not use runtime:sleep() in workflows.

```ballerina
check ctx.sleep({seconds: 30});
```

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: The duration to sleep

return.description: An error if the sleep fails, otherwise nil

functions.name: currentTime
functions.description:
Returns the deterministic workflow time. Use instead of `time:utcNow()` inside workflows.

```ballerina
time:Utc now = ctx.currentTime();
```

return.description: The current workflow time as `time:Utc`

functions.name: isReplaying
functions.description: Checks whether the workflow is recovering from a failure (re-executing recorded history).

return.description: `true` if recovering, `false` on first execution

functions.name: getWorkflowId
functions.description: Get the unique workflow ID.

return.description: The workflow ID

functions.name: getWorkflowType
functions.description: Get the workflow type name.

return.description: The workflow type

parameters.name: futures
parameters.description: Data futures from the workflow's events record

parameters.name: minCount

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum wait duration; returns an error on timeout

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected return type, inferred from how the result is assigned

return.description: Positional tuple of values (`nil` for an incomplete position), or an error

parameters.name: userRoles

functions.name: runChildWorkflow
functions.description:
Starts a child workflow and returns its instance ID without waiting for the result.
The child is a true Temporal child workflow: its lifecycle is tied to this workflow,
so when this workflow closes, in-flight children are cancelled with it.

Use `getChildWorkflowResult` (non-blocking) or `waitForChildWorkflow` (durable wait)
to read the child's result later — this enables fan-out/fan-in orchestration:

```ballerina
string kycId = check ctx->runChildWorkflow(kycWorkflow, input = customer);   // fan out
string scoreId = check ctx->runChildWorkflow(scoreWorkflow, input = customer);
Kyc kyc = check ctx->waitForChildWorkflow(kycId);                            // gather
Score score = check ctx->waitForChildWorkflow(scoreId);
```

parameters.name: childWorkflow
parameters.description: The child workflow function (must have `@Workflow`)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description:
Optional input for the child workflow. Must match the child workflow
function's declared input parameter type (any `anydata` subtype)

return.description: The child workflow instance ID, or an error if the child could not start

functions.name: getChildWorkflowResult
functions.description:
Returns the result of a child workflow started with `runChildWorkflow` if it has
already completed, without waiting. While the child is still running (e.g. suspended
on a human task) a `workflow:WorkflowBusyError` is returned — check back later, or
switch to the blocking `waitForChildWorkflow` form.

```ballerina
Kyc|error result = ctx->getChildWorkflowResult(kycId);
if result is workflow:WorkflowBusyError { /* still running — do other work */ }
```

parameters.name: childWorkflowId
parameters.description: The child workflow instance ID returned by `runChildWorkflow`

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected result type (inferred from context)

return.description:
The child's result as `T`, a `workflow:WorkflowBusyError` while the child
is still running, or an error if the child failed

functions.name: waitForChildWorkflow
functions.description:
Waits durably until a child workflow started with `runChildWorkflow` completes and
returns its result. The wait is a durable suspend — no thread is held, and the wait
survives worker crashes and restarts (on replay the result is served from history).

parameters.name: childWorkflowId
parameters.description: The child workflow instance ID returned by `runChildWorkflow`

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected result type (inferred from context)

return.description: The child's result as `T`, or an error if the child failed

functions.name: callWorkflow
functions.description:
Starts a child workflow and durably waits for its result — `runChildWorkflow`
followed by `waitForChildWorkflow` fused into one call. "Blocking" here is a durable
suspend, not a held thread, so this is safe for long-running children.

```ballerina
Receipt receipt = check ctx->callWorkflow(billingWorkflow, input = order);
```

parameters.name: childWorkflow
parameters.description: The child workflow function (must have `@Workflow`)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description:
Optional input for the child workflow. Must match the child workflow
function's declared input parameter type (any `anydata` subtype)

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Expected result type (inferred from context)

return.description: The child's result as `T`, or an error if the child failed

functions.name: sendDataToChildWorkflow
functions.description:
Sends data to a running workflow instance's events record from inside a workflow.
This is the in-workflow counterpart of `workflow:sendData` and is typically used to
signal a child workflow started with `runChildWorkflow`, but accepts any workflow
instance ID.

```ballerina
check ctx->sendDataToChildWorkflow(childId, "approval", {approved: true});
```

parameters.name: childWorkflowId
parameters.description: Target workflow instance ID (usually from `runChildWorkflow`)

parameters.name: dataName
parameters.description: Field name in the target workflow's events record

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data payload

return.description: An error if sending fails

functions.name: completeHumanTask
functions.description:
Completes a pending human task by sending the result back to the waiting workflow.
The `taskWorkflowId` is the child workflow ID of the task, which is
available via the inbox/task-listing API and is composed as:
`"humantask-<parentWorkflowId>-<taskName>-<uuid>"`.

```ballerina
check workflow:completeHumanTask(taskWorkflowId, {approved: true, comment: "LGTM"});
```

If `callerRoles` is provided the function fetches the `userRoles` stored on the task
and returns an error when none of the caller's roles appear in that list.
When omitted the role check is skipped; enforcement is then the caller's responsibility.

parameters.name: taskWorkflowId
parameters.description: Temporal workflow ID of the human task child workflow

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: The value to return to the workflow (must be compatible with the declared `T`)

parameters.name: callerRoles
parameters.description: Roles held by the caller; validated against the task's configured `userRoles`

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user ID of the person completing the task (used for auditing)

return.description: An error if the task cannot be found, is already completed, or the caller is unauthorized
